Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Our opening proposal is a substantial, straightforward recovery for the class, distributed automatically using Brightline’s records. The proposed fee is separate from the class fund, and any portion the court does not award should benefit the class rather than return to Brightline.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Brightline is prepared to offer a substantial, automatically distributed recovery, but your proposal exceeds its authorized all-in settlement limit. Our counter is $27 million for the class and $8 million in fees, with unawarded fees reverting to Brightline. Brightline will agree to clear sailing on the fee request, subject to court approval.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate Brightline’s substantial offer and its commitment to automatic distribution. We propose keeping the fund, fee, clear-sailing, and distribution terms unchanged, but providing that any portion of the fee the court does not award goes to the class rather than reverting to Brightline. This preserves the package while ensuring court-declined fees benefit members.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Brightline accepts your latest term sheet, subject to court approval.

private_notes.private_reasoning: Open with a strong but supportable anchor reflecting the $64 million in disputed charges, the merits of the case, and the low-friction ability to pay identified members automatically. Seek meaningful fees for the substantial contingency investment, while protecting class members if the court awards less than requested. Do not accept any term sheet yet.

Need make a credible counteroffer below Brightline’s $40 million all-in cap, preserving room to negotiate. Automatic distribution is valuable given complete records. Offer $27 million for the class and $8 million in fees, with fees reverting if not awarded; total maximum outlay is $35 million. Clear sailing can help secure agreement, while the offer remains materially below counsel’s $57 million demand.

The offered $27 million automatic class recovery and $8 million fee are a substantial package. I should preserve the class’s automatic payment and seek a no-cost improvement: any fee the court declines should go to the class, not back to Brightline. I will not accept the current term sheet as written.

The latest term sheet totals $35 million, below Brightline’s $40 million all-in authorization. It also provides automatic payments to identified members and resolves the only remaining disagreement: court-declined fees benefit the class rather than reverting to Brightline. Accepting secures a court-approval path within the authorized cap.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement: The settlement was reached through arm’s-length negotiations in confidential mediation. Consistent with the confidentiality of those communications, I do not recount specific offers or mediation discussions here. The resulting agreement provides for automatic distribution of the class fund and makes any fee amount not approved by the Court available to the class rather than returning it to Brightline.
